findings.summary: Encoded Reader structure matching rejects double-encoded fixed markers before they stabilize.
findings.consequence: A path such as `/forfattare/A/%2574itlar/<201-char-title>/sida/1/etext` is classified as non-Reader while selecting the parser title cap, then decodes into a Reader-shaped segment list. The current middleware still rejects the oversized title through `normalizeLegacyRouteIdentity(..., 200)` before resolver I/O, so the observable route remains protected, but the exported parser and structure classifier do not consistently enforce their own Reader title boundary for stable multi-pass encodings.
findings.evidence: `decodedEquals` delegates to `decodeStable(raw, expected.length)`, so `%2574itlar` decodes first to `%74itlar` and is rejected because that intermediate string length is 8 while `expected.length` is 6. A read-only Node probe of the same helper logic returned `decodedEquals: false` and `rawLegacyReaderShape: false` for `%2574itlar`, even though a later full decode yields `titlar`. The listed unit and SSR tests cover a single-encoded fixed marker but not the double-encoded case.
findings.recommendation: For fixed structural marker comparison, keep the raw length guard but allow escaped intermediate forms to stabilize before the final equality check, or decode fixed positions once with a structural-marker-specific helper that compares only the stable final value to the expected token.
